nodes.label: Imperative migrations workflow
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Iterate with execute_sql / supabase db query; never apply_migration locally because it writes history on every call and breaks db diff/pull. Commit via advisors, checklist review, db pull, migration list.

nodes.label: Recover from errors, don't loop
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: After 2-3 failed attempts, change method, check docs and logs instead of retrying the same command.

nodes.author: supabase

nodes.label: Verify your work with a test query
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: verify your work with a test query

nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: use app_metadata, never user_metadata, for authorization
nodes.rationale: raw_user_meta_data is user-editable and appears in auth.jwt(); JWT claims may be stale until token refresh.

nodes.label: auth.role() deprecated in favour of TO clause
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: auth.role() deprecated in favour of to clause
nodes.rationale: auth.role() = 'authenticated' also passes anonymous sign-ins, which carry the authenticated role.

nodes.label: TO authenticated needs an ownership predicate (BOLA/IDOR)
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: to authenticated needs an ownership predicate (bola/idor)
nodes.rationale: Role check is authentication without authorization; combine with (select auth.uid()) = user_id.

nodes.label: Supabase security checklist
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Supabase-specific traps that silently create vulnerabilities across auth, keys, RLS, views, storage and dependencies.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER functions bypass RLS
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Never add it to fix a permission error; prefer SECURITY INVOKER. In public it is callable by anon/authenticated via PUBLIC EXECUTE, so keep it in a non-exposed schema with an auth.uid() check.

nodes.label: Views bypass RLS (use security_invoker)
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: On Postgres 15+ use WITH (security_invoker = true); otherwise revoke anon/authenticated or use an unexposed schema.

nodes.label: Never expose service_role key in public clients
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: never expose service_role key in public clients
nodes.rationale: Prefer publishable keys; any NEXT_PUBLIC_ env var is sent to the browser.

nodes.label: Deleting a user does not invalidate access tokens
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: deleting a user does not invalidate access tokens
nodes.rationale: Revoke sessions first, keep JWT expiry short, validate session_id against auth.sessions for strict guarantees.

nodes.label: Storage upsert needs INSERT + SELECT + UPDATE
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: storage upsert needs insert + select + update
nodes.rationale: INSERT alone allows uploads but file replacement silently fails.

nodes.label: UPDATE requires a SELECT policy
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Without a SELECT policy updates silently affect 0 rows.

nodes.label: UPDATE policies need USING and WITH CHECK
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: update policies need using and with check
nodes.rationale: Without WITH CHECK a user can reassign a row's user_id to someone else.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres Best Practices Skill
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Rules are grouped into 8 categories prioritized by impact (CRITICAL query/connection/security down to LOW advanced features) so agents fix the highest-impact issues first; must be loaded before any schema, migration, RLS, index or SQL change, not only for performance work.

nodes.label: auth.uid()
nodes.rationale: Supabase function returning the authenticated user's id for policies.

nodes.label: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
nodes.rationale: Applies RLS even to the table owner.

nodes.label: Row Level Security (RLS)
nodes.rationale: Policies enforce per-user row access in the database rather than the application.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER helper function
nodes.rationale: Bypasses RLS for internal lookups; keep in a private schema, set search_path='', check auth.uid() inside, revoke EXECUTE.

nodes.label: Apply Principle of Least Privilege
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM: reduced attack surface and better audit trail; never use superuser for app queries.

nodes.label: Enable Row Level Security for Multi-Tenant Data
nodes.norm_label: enable row level security for multi-tenant data
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL: database-enforced tenant isolation; app-level filtering alone leaks all data on a bug.

nodes.label: Optimize RLS Policies for Performance
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: 5-10x faster RLS queries with subqueries and indexes.

nodes.label: Principle of least privilege
nodes.rationale: Broad grants make any SQL injection catastrophic.

nodes.label: Index RLS policy columns
nodes.rationale: Always index columns referenced by RLS policies, e.g. orders(user_id).

nodes.label: (select auth.uid()) wrapped call
nodes.rationale: Wrapping in SELECT evaluates once and caches instead of per row (100x+ on large tables).

nodes.label: Buffers shared hit vs read
nodes.rationale: read >> hit means data is not cached and needs more memory.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: Executes the query and reports actual timings and buffer usage, revealing the real bottleneck.

nodes.label: Seq Scan (sequential scan)
nodes.rationale: A Seq Scan on a large table, with many 'Rows Removed by Filter', signals a missing index.

nodes.label: work_mem
nodes.rationale: 'Sort Method: external merge' indicates work_mem is too low.

nodes.label: ANALYZE (planner statistics)
nodes.rationale: Updates statistics so the planner picks Index Scan over Seq Scan correctly; run after large data changes.

nodes.label: pg_stat_user_tables
nodes.rationale: Shows last_vacuum/last_analyze timestamps per table.

nodes.label: VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Reclaims space from dead tuples.

nodes.label: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries
nodes.norm_label: use explain analyze to diagnose slow queries
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW-MEDIUM: identify exact bottlenecks instead of guessing which index is missing.

nodes.label: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
nodes.norm_label: maintain table statistics with vacuum and analyze
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM: 2-10x better query plans; stale statistics make the planner choose wrong strategies.

nodes.label: Add Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.norm_label: add indexes on where and join columns
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL: 100-1000x faster queries; unindexed filters/joins cause full table scans that worsen as tables grow.

nodes.label: Autovacuum scale factor tuning
nodes.rationale: Lower autovacuum_vacuum/analyze_scale_factor (5%/2% vs 20%/10% defaults) on high-churn tables.

nodes.label: Index WHERE and JOIN columns
nodes.rationale: Index frequently filtered columns and always the foreign-key side of a JOIN.

nodes.label: Security Checklist (SECURITY DEFINER, auth.role() deprecation, BOLA)
nodes.norm_label: security checklist (security definer, auth.role() deprecation, bola)

nodes.label: Impact Level Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Maps impact levels to expected gains: CRITICAL 10-100x, HIGH 5-20x, MEDIUM-HIGH 2-5x, MEDIUM 1.5-3x, LOW-MEDIUM 1.2-2x, LOW incremental.

nodes.label: jsonb_path_ops Operator Class
nodes.rationale: Supports only @> but yields a 2-3x smaller index than the default jsonb_ops.

nodes.label: Session Mode Pooling
nodes.rationale: Connection held for the whole session; needed for prepared statements and temp tables (Supabase port 5432 vs 6543).

nodes.label: Transaction Mode Pooling
nodes.rationale: Connection returned after each transaction; best for most apps but breaks named prepared statements.

nodes.label: Writing Guidelines for Postgres References
nodes.rationale: Default to SQL-only examples for portability; include application code only for pooling config, transaction management, ORM N+1 anti-patterns and prepared statement usage.

nodes.label: Section Definitions
nodes.rationale: Rules are assigned to sections automatically by filename prefix.

nodes.label: Rule Reference Template
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter carries title, impact, impactDescription and tags; body is a 1-2 sentence explanation, an Incorrect example, a Correct example, optional trade-offs, and a reference link.

nodes.label: Concrete Transformation Patterns
nodes.rationale: Show exact SQL rewrites rather than philosophical advice.

nodes.label: Error-First Structure
nodes.rationale: Showing the problematic pattern before the solution trains agents to recognize anti-patterns.

nodes.label: Quantified Impact
nodes.rationale: Specific metrics (10x faster, 50% smaller index) help agents prioritize fixes; vague words like 'faster' do not.

nodes.label: Use tsvector for Full-Text Search
nodes.rationale: LIKE with leading wildcards cannot use indexes; a generated tsvector column with a GIN index is ~100x faster and supports ranking via ts_rank.

nodes.label: Index JSONB Columns for Efficient Querying
nodes.norm_label: index jsonb columns for efficient querying
nodes.rationale: Unindexed JSONB queries full-scan; GIN covers containment operators and expression indexes cover single-key lookups (10-100x faster).

nodes.label: Configure Idle Connection Timeouts
nodes.rationale: Idle and idle-in-transaction sessions waste slots and hold locks; timeouts reclaim 30-50% of connection slots. Pooled setups configure this at the pooler.

nodes.label: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
nodes.rationale: Each connection costs 1-3MB RAM; size max_connections from available memory (100-200 for 4GB) and keep work_mem * max_connections under 25% of RAM.

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications
nodes.rationale: Connections are expensive; a pooler lets many clients share a small pool (pool_size = cores*2 + spindles), handling 10-100x more concurrent users.

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling
nodes.rationale: Prepared statements are per-connection, so transaction-mode pooling causes 'does not exist' errors; use unnamed statements, deallocate, or session mode (e.g. Node pg prepare:false, JDBC prepareThreshold=0).

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data
nodes.rationale: Each single-row insert is a round trip and transaction; multi-row VALUES (~1000 rows/batch) is 10-50x faster.

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading
nodes.rationale: Per-item queries in a loop cost one round trip each; use = any($1::bigint[]) or a JOIN for 10-100x fewer round trips.

nodes.label: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.norm_label: use cursor-based pagination instead of offset
nodes.rationale: OFFSET scans every skipped row; keyset pagination on indexed sort columns (including all sort columns in the cursor) is constant-time at any depth.

nodes.label: Use UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT)
nodes.rationale: SELECT-then-INSERT races and hits duplicate key errors; ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE / DO NOTHING is atomic.

nodes.label: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.norm_label: use advisory locks for application-level locking
nodes.rationale: pg_advisory_lock / pg_advisory_xact_lock / pg_try_advisory_lock coordinate work without dummy lock rows or row-lock overhead.

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering
nodes.rationale: Deadlocks come from acquiring locks in different orders; lock rows up front ordered by id (SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE) or update atomically in one statement.

nodes.label: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention
nodes.rationale: Holding locks across external calls (e.g. payment APIs) blocks other queries; do external work outside the transaction for 3-5x throughput and fewer deadlocks.

nodes.label: Use SKIP LOCKED for Non-Blocking Queue Processing
nodes.norm_label: use skip locked for non-blocking queue processing
nodes.rationale: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lets parallel workers claim different queue rows without waiting (10x throughput); combine with UPDATE ... WHERE id = (subquery) for atomic claim.

nodes.label: BRIN index
nodes.rationale: Large time-series tables; 10-100x smaller than B-tree.

nodes.label: B-tree index
nodes.rationale: Default; supports =, <, >, BETWEEN, IN, IS NULL but not JSONB @>.

nodes.label: GIN index
nodes.rationale: For arrays, JSONB (@>, ?, ?&, ?|) and full-text search.

nodes.label: GiST index
nodes.rationale: Geometric data, range types, nearest-neighbor (KNN).

nodes.label: Hash index
nodes.rationale: Equality-only; slightly faster than B-tree for =.

nodes.label: Drop partition for data retention
nodes.rationale: Dropping an old partition is instant versus an hours-long DELETE.

nodes.label: Partition pruning
nodes.rationale: Queries scan only the partitions matching the predicate.

nodes.label: Range partitioning by time
nodes.rationale: partition by range (created_at) with monthly partitions.

nodes.label: Choose the Right Index Type for Your Data
nodes.norm_label: choose the right index type for your data
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: 10-100x improvement; the default B-tree is not always optimal.

nodes.label: Partition Large Tables for Better Performance
nodes.norm_label: partition large tables for better performance
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM-HIGH: 5-20x faster queries and maintenance; partition tables >100M rows or time-series data.

nodes.label: Bitmap scan combining separate indexes
nodes.rationale: Slower path when separate single-column indexes must be combined.

nodes.label: Composite (multi-column) index
nodes.rationale: One index on (status, created_at) beats two single-column indexes combined via bitmap scan.

nodes.label: Covering index (INCLUDE)
nodes.rationale: INCLUDE columns that are selected but not filtered on so the query never touches the heap.

nodes.label: Index-only scan
nodes.rationale: Serves all needed columns from the index, skipping the table entirely.

nodes.label: Create Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
nodes.norm_label: create composite indexes for multi-column queries
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: 5-10x faster multi-column queries.

nodes.label: Use Covering Indexes to Avoid Table Lookups
nodes.norm_label: use covering indexes to avoid table lookups
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM-HIGH: 2-5x faster queries by eliminating heap fetches.

nodes.label: Leftmost prefix rule
nodes.rationale: Place equality columns first, range columns last; index is unusable for filters that skip the leading column.

nodes.label: ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS (unsupported)
nodes.rationale: Postgres has no such syntax; it fails with SQLSTATE 42601.

nodes.label: Add Constraints Safely in Migrations
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: prevents migration failures and enables idempotent schema changes.

nodes.label: Choose Appropriate Data Types
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: 50% storage reduction, faster comparisons, fewer bugs.

nodes.label: Idempotent constraint DO block
nodes.rationale: Check pg_constraint inside a DO $$ block before ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT; works for unique, check, FK.

nodes.label: numeric for money
nodes.rationale: Exact decimal arithmetic; float loses precision.

nodes.label: text over varchar(n)
nodes.rationale: No artificial limit, same performance as varchar.

nodes.label: timestamptz over timestamp
nodes.rationale: Always store timezone-aware timestamps.

nodes.label: bigint generated always as identity
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard, sequential, 8 bytes; best for a single database.

nodes.label: serial
nodes.rationale: Works, but identity is SQL-standard and preferred.

nodes.label: Time-prefixed text IDs
nodes.rationale: Sortable distributed IDs without an extension (timestamp prefix + gen_random_uuid).

nodes.label: Random UUIDv4 primary keys
nodes.rationale: Random values scatter inserts and fragment the index on large tables.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 (pg_uuidv7)
nodes.rationale: Time-ordered UUIDs for distributed/exposed IDs without fragmentation.

nodes.label: Select Optimal Primary Key Strategy
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: better index locality and less fragmentation; PK choice affects inserts, index size, replication.

nodes.label: bigint IDs over int
nodes.rationale: int overflows at 2.1 billion; bigint is future-proof.

nodes.label: pg_constraint catalog
nodes.rationale: contype p=PRIMARY KEY, f=FOREIGN KEY, u=UNIQUE, c=CHECK.

nodes.label: Foreign key column index
nodes.rationale: Always index the referencing column so JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE use an index scan.

nodes.label: Missing FK index detection query
nodes.rationale: Joins pg_constraint (contype='f') with pg_attribute and checks pg_index for coverage.

nodes.label: ON DELETE CASCADE
nodes.rationale: Without an FK index the cascade locks and scans the whole child table.

nodes.label: Index Foreign Key Columns
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; missing indexes slow JOINs and CASCADE deletes.

nodes.label: Compatibility view layer
nodes.rationale: If stuck with mixed case, expose a lowercase view aliasing the quoted columns.

nodes.label: Quoted mixed-case identifiers
nodes.rationale: Require quotes forever; often produced by ORMs, migrations, GUI tools.

nodes.label: Use Lowercase Identifiers for Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM: avoids case-sensitivity bugs with tools, ORMs and AI assistants.

nodes.label: Lowercase snake_case identifiers
nodes.rationale: Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase; unquoted snake_case is portable.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements extension
nodes.rationale: Tracks execution stats (calls, total/mean exec time) for all queries to find slow and frequent ones.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements_reset()
nodes.rationale: Reset statistics after optimizing to measure the effect.

nodes.label: Enable pg_stat_statements for Query Analysis
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW-MEDIUM: without it there is no visibility into which queries consume resources.

nodes.label: Partial index (WHERE clause)
nodes.rationale: Indexes only rows matching a predicate, e.g. active users, pending orders, non-null SKUs.

nodes.label: Use Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries
nodes.norm_label: use partial indexes for filtered queries
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH: 5-20x smaller indexes, faster writes and queries when queries consistently filter the same condition.
